title: TCP Handshake, Byte-Stream Sequence/ACK Numbers, Flow Control, FIN & RST
topic: TCP 3-Way Handshake, Seq/Ack, Sliding Window, Retransmissions, FIN vs. RST, Multi-Flow
learning_objectives: Trace SYN, SYN+ACK, and ACK packets and verify sequence/acknowledgement number progression.
Distinguish graceful connection termination (FIN/ACK) from abrupt termination (RST) and refused connections (ECONNREFUSED).
Analyze multiple concurrent TCP flows using bidirectional 4-tuple isolation.

concept_explanation.title: Three-Way Handshake & Byte-Stream Numbering
concept_explanation.summary: TCP establishes synchronized full-duplex state with SYN -> SYN+ACK -> ACK. Sequence numbers count transmitted stream bytes (plus 1 phantom byte for SYN and FIN), NOT message IDs.
key_points: SYN carries the sender's Initial Sequence Number (ISN); the peer acknowledges with ACK = ISN + 1.
When a segment carries L payload bytes starting at sequence S, the receiver's cumulative ACK advances to S + L.
The advertised TCP window size implements receiver-driven flow control.

concept_explanation.title: Graceful FIN vs. Abrupt RST Termination
concept_explanation.summary: TCP closes each sending half independently with FIN/ACK. In contrast, RST immediately aborts a connection (e.g., connecting to a closed port or closing with SO_LINGER timeout=0).
key_points: Connecting to an unbound port produces a kernel RST+ACK packet and ECONNREFUSED in connect().
Multiple concurrent clients create separate 4-tuple flows distinguished by their ephemeral client ports.

experiment.title: Run Controlled TCP Protocol Scenarios (Complete, Refused, Multi-Transfer, RST, Multi-Flow)
experiment.instructions: Select a TCP scenario below and execute it. NetBox captures real socket API calls and real TCP packets on loopback, runs the Phase 4 TCP flow analyzer, and lets you interrogate the exact packets with the Grounded Local AI Assistant.
required_setup: Phase 4 libpcap packet capture helper with cap_net_raw
execution_steps: Run 'Complete TCP Echo' and inspect the 3-way handshake, PSH+ACK data packets, and FIN termination in the Packets & TCP Flows tabs.
Run 'Connection Refused (Closed Port)' and observe SYN -> RST+ACK and ECONNREFUSED.
Run 'Abrupt Termination (RST)' and 'Multiple Concurrent Flows' to compare graceful vs. abrupt close and multi-flow isolation.

supported_scenarios.label: 1. Complete TCP Handshake & Graceful FIN
supported_scenarios.description: Standard TCP echo with 3-way handshake, bidirectional data transfer, and graceful FIN/ACK teardown.

supported_scenarios.label: 2. Failed Connection (ECONNREFUSED / RST)
supported_scenarios.description: Client connects to a closed localhost port; observes real ECONNREFUSED socket error and kernel RST+ACK packet.

supported_scenarios.label: 3. Multiple Data Transfers on One Flow
supported_scenarios.description: Sends 4 sequential application chunks on one TCP connection to observe cumulative sequence/ACK progression.

supported_scenarios.label: 4. Abrupt Termination (TCP RST via SO_LINGER)
supported_scenarios.description: Establishes TCP connection, exchanges data, then aborts abruptly with a real TCP RST packet.

supported_scenarios.label: 5. Multiple Concurrent TCP Flows
supported_scenarios.description: Two concurrent TCP clients connect to the server simultaneously so students inspect 2 distinct 4-tuple flows.

expected_observations: Complete TCP echo shows handshake status COMPLETE (SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK) and COMPLETE_FIN_EXCHANGE.
Connection refused shows connect() returning -1 (ECONNREFUSED) and RST packet with incomplete handshake.
Multi-flow scenario produces 2 distinct flow_ids with distinct client ephemeral ports.
observation_caveats: TCP sequence numbers are absolute 32-bit integers on the wire; compare adjacent packet deltas to verify byte-stream progression.
Localhost loopback rarely drops packets, so retransmissions are normally 0 unless artificially induced.

questions.prompt: A client sends a TCP PSH+ACK segment with seq=1001 and payload_length=29. Assuming no packet loss, what acknowledgement number should the server send back?
questions.rubric_summary: Cumulative ACK = received sequence number + payload length = 1001 + 29 = 1030.
questions.explanation: TCP ACKs indicate the next expected byte offset in the stream: 1001 + 29 = 1030.

questions.prompt: What happens at the packet layer when a TCP client calls connect() to a localhost port where no server is listening?
options: The server accepts the connection and immediately sends FIN.
The client sends SYN, the kernel replies with RST+ACK, and connect() fails with ECONNREFUSED.
The OS automatically switches the socket to UDP.
No packet is transmitted on loopback.
questions.rubric_summary: Kernel responds to SYN on an unbound port with RST+ACK, surfacing ECONNREFUSED.
questions.explanation: TCP rejects connection attempts to closed ports by replying with RST+ACK, causing the client's connect() syscall to return -1 with errno=ECONNREFUSED.

questions.prompt: Why does TCP need a separate FIN from BOTH endpoints for graceful full-duplex teardown, unlike a single RST?
questions.rubric_summary: TCP is full-duplex; each FIN closes only one sending direction while allowing buffered peer data to finish.
questions.explanation: Because TCP is full-duplex, one endpoint's FIN only signals it has no more data to send (half-close); the peer may still finish sending data before sending its own FIN. RST aborts both directions immediately.
